newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Costello says bank mergers more than one year away.
newsitem.headline: Costello says bank mergers more than one year away.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Sunday that it would be at least one year before the government would permit the nation's big four private banks to consider merging with one another.
Costello said the banking sector would have to become more competitive before such mergers would be approved.

The big four banks are the National Australia Bank Ltd, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Westpac Banking Corp and the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd. Each has assets of more than A$100 billion.

Interviewed about the policy implications of the Wallis Inquiry into the financial system, Costello said the competitive changes proposed in the Wallis report would have to be put in place before large scale mergers could proceed.

"Now if the Wallis recommendations were implemented it would be more competitive in my view but that's going to take a while so we're looking at a situation where I wouldn't imagine any change within the year," he said on the Nine Network's Business Sunday programme.
"Maybe two (years), maybe longer, it depends on getting those competitive arrangements in force."

When Costello released the Wallis report last Wednesday, he focussed on the need for the banking sector to provide better services to the small business sector as a prerequisite for allowing big bank mergers.

He did, however, approve the end of the "six pillars" policy which prevented mergers between the big banks and the nation's two largest insurance firms -- the AMP Society and National Mutual Holdings Ltd.

Costello also accepted the Wallis report's recommendation that the blanket ban on foreign bank takeovers be abandoned in favour of a case-by-case basis and a strong commitment to national interest guidelines.

Brokers and investors have speculated for the last year or so that the Wallis inquiry would approve the end of the six pillars policy but were surprised by the government's decision last week to impose a continued ban on the big four banks.

Westpac, which many analysts had thought would be a target of NAB, fell sharply after the report was released as did ANZ but the latter bank has now become the subject of market speculation that it may be targeted by a foreign bank such as Lloyds TSB or ABN Amro. Westpac and ANZ each have a market capitalisation of about A$11.6 billion.
